findings: 315 trend tests run. The usual test reports 313 pixels at p < 0.05; after removing month-to-month stickiness, 305 remain at p < 0.05, and 310 pass false-discovery control (10% across every test in this box). Separately, 5 cluster(s) are larger than the largest cluster on 95% of time-shuffled maps of all variables.
Rainfall: drier across 63 pixels around -10.0N, -61.9E (-0.587 mm/day per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Wind speed at 2 m: calmer across 59 pixels around -9.9N, -61.9E (-0.0068 m/s per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Air temperature: warming across 63 pixels around -10.0N, -61.9E (+0.446 degC per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Relative humidity: less humid across 58 pixels around -10.2N, -61.9E (-1.79 % per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Root-zone soil wetness: drying soil across 62 pixels around -10.0N, -61.8E (-0.0264 0-1 per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Compound pattern: Warming and drier in the same place (63 pixels) near -10.0N, -61.9E.
Compound pattern: Warming and drying soil in the same place (62 pixels) near -10.0N, -61.8E.
Compound pattern: Drier and drying soil in the same place (62 pixels) near -10.0N, -61.8E.
Trend regimes found by clustering: drier + warming + less humid (27 pixels); drier + calmer + warming (36 pixels).
caveats: NASA POWER here is MERRA-2-based reanalysis at about 0.5 degrees: a model constrained by observations, not a direct measurement.
Reanalysis can contain sudden jumps when the satellites feeding it change; a trend can partly be such a jump, especially for wind.
Linear trends only. Clusters show where change is stronger than chance, not why it happened.
